lake.DESCRIPT: Simple two story lakes are characterized by simple fish communities, typically with fewer than 4 different groups of sportfish present (e.g., panfish, bass, and trout). They are small in area but deep, cold, and well-oxygenated with good water quality. There are 58 simple two story lakes in Wisconsin, scattered across all parts of the state but most in the north.
lake.FISHERIES: Simple two story lakes can support good action for smallmouth bass, and the cold, well-oxygenated deep layer can support trout populations.

lake.DESCRIPT: Complex riverine lakes are characterized by complex fish communities, typically with 4 or more different groups of sportfish present. Water tends to flow though these lakes quickly (on average less than 15 day residence-time), so they can function similarly to rivers, and often have relatively low clarity. There are 183 complex riverine lakes in Wisconsin, scattered across all parts of the state.
lake.FISHERIES: Complex riverine lakes often support great fisheries for riverine species like smallmouth bass, and in some systems, walleye.

lake.DESCRIPT: Simple warm dark lakes are characterized by simple fish communities, typically with fewer than 4 different groups of sportfish (e.g., panfish and some bass or northern pike). Water temperatures tend to be warmer than average, and water is less clear than average. They tend to be small in surface area.  This is the most common class of lake in Wisconsin, with 1,650 simple warm dark lakes  scattered across all parts of the state.
lake.FISHERIES: Simple warm dark lakes can provide great opportunities for action for black crappie, and often also support bluegill and largemouth bass. They rarely have any walleye or muskellunge.

lake.DESCRIPT: Simple harsh lakes are lakes where extreme conditions, typically winterkills, limit what fish can survive. They are broken into two categories: "has fishery" and "no fishery". This lake is in the "simple harsh - no fishery" class where winterkills are frequently and lake pH is very low, so few fish can survive. They are very small in surface area. There are 1,059 of these lakes scattered around the state.
lake.FISHERIES: "Simple harsh - no fishery" lakes usually have not sportfish species present. Central mudminnow and small minnow species are typically the only species that can survive in these lakes.

Water tends to flow though these lakes quickly (on average less than 15 day residence-time) and they tend to be small in surface area - many of these are small millponds on warmwater streams. There are 175 simple riverine lakes in Wisconsin, scattered across all parts of the state.

Simple trout ponds are characterized by simple fish communities, typically with fewer than 4 different groups of sportfish present (e.g., panfish, bass, and trout). These tend to be shallow and small in surface area, and springs that provide incoming groundwater keep temperatures cold and suitable for trout. There are 308 simple trout ponds in the state, mostly in the northern part of the state and concentrated in and around Langlade county.

lake_fish: "Simple harsh - has fishery" lakes may have some panfish, particularly yellow perch, and can be dominated by bullheads.
"Simple harsh - no fishery" lakes usually have not sportfish species present. Central mudminnow and small minnow species are typically the only species that can survive in these lakes.
Complex cool clear lakes can often support quality or action walleye fisheries, and can have great action fisheries for smallmouth bass.

Complex cool dark lakes can often support quality or action walleye fisheries, and can have great action fisheries for yellow perch, and have the potential to produce quality northern pike and muskellunge fisheries.
Complex riverine lakes often support great fisheries for riverine species like smallmouth bass, and in some systems, walleye.

Complex two story lakes are able to support coldwater species - primarily cisco, and occasionally lake trout or lake whitefish. They have the potential to produce action and quality walleye fisheries.
Complex warm clear lakes often support great action fisheries for warmwater species like bluegill and largemouth bass.
Complex warm dark lakes often support great action fisheries for black crappie, and have potential to produced quality walleye, northern pike, and/or muskellunge fisheries.
Simple cool clear lakes can have good action for black crappie and northern pike, moderate action for yellow perch, and rarely have any walleye or muskellunge
Simple cool clear lakes can have good action for smallmouth bass, and rarely have any walleye or muskellunge
Simple riverine lakes may have good action opportunities for smallmouth bass and quality opportunities for northern pike. They rarely have any walleye or muskellunge.
Simple trout ponds may have some warmwater species like bluegill, pumpkinseed, largemouth bass, or northern pike present, but also can support coldwater-dependent trout species.

Simple warm clear lakes can provide great opportunities for action and quality for largemouth bass and bluegill. They rarely have any walleye or muskellunge.
